plan.title: sec: triage cache + init/update projection writers follow repo-controlled symlinks outside the checkout

narratives.Description: This story implements the cited GitHub issue acceptance criteria in the scoped packages listed in swarm.file_scope. It includes regression tests and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased Fixed or Changed as appropriate.
narratives.Overview:
**Severity:** Medium (2 findings)
**Source:** Scheduled application-security review at `6e288a2de499cadfce43e176a7b08c5d15d52d4f`
**Related:** same trust-boundary class as #2413 (MAP / gitignore / gitattributes projection containment), #2383 (installer consumer projections), and #2305 / #2407 (deposit symlink escape)

## Summary

Two TypeScript engine write paths still follow repo-controlled symlinks when resolving lifecycle/cache state or depositing installer-managed projections. A malicious repository author can commit a symlink at a well-known path; a routine operator/agent command then creates, appends, overwrites, or chmods an attacker-chosen writable file **outside** the project tree.

`assertProjectionContained` (#2413) already guards newer projection surfaces; these two call sites were not covered.

---

### 1) Medium — Runtime triage/lifecycle state writes follow a repo-controlled `xbrief` symlink outside the checkout

**Location:** `packages/core/src/triage/cache-path.ts`

**Attacker / input:** a malicious repository author commits `xbrief` as a symlink to an existing writable directory outside the project.

**Attack path:**
1. Victim clones the repo and runs routine commands such as `task doctor`, `task triage:summary`, or scope lifecycle actions.
2. Those commands call the layout-aware triage cache resolver.
3. The resolver resolves or falls back to `<project>/xbrief/.triage-cache` without an `lstat` / `realpath` containment check.
4. Downstream writers then `mkdirSync`, `appendFileSync`, or `writeFileSync` the returned paths.

**Impact:** creates or appends Deft state files such as `summary-history.jsonl`, `doctor-state.json`, `scope-lifecycle.jsonl`, and lock files outside the repository under the victim account.

**Remediation:** make lifecycle/cache path resolution reject symlinked `xbrief` / `.triage-cache` components that escape the real project root before any mkdir/read/write.

---

### 2) Medium — TS-native directive init/update projection writers follow repo-controlled symlinks outside the checkout

**Location:** `packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts`

**Attacker / input:** a malicious repository author commits installer-managed projection paths such as `AGENTS.md`, `Taskfile.yml`, `.agents/`, `.githooks/`, `.github/codeql/`, `greptile.json`, or `.gitattributes` as symlinks to writable paths outside the checkout.

**Attack path:**
1. Victim clones the repo and runs init/update (`runInitDeposit` / `runRefreshDeposit`).
2. Those call `writeAgentsMd`, `writeAgentsSkills`, `depositNeutralization`, `writeConsumerVbrief`, `writeConsumerGitHooks`, and `ensureTaskfile`.
3. Helpers build destinations with `join(projectDir, ...)` and use `mkdirSync`, `writeFileSync`, `copyFileSync`, or `chmodSync` without the projection containment guard used by newer projection surfaces.

**Impact:** routine init/update can overwrite, create, or chmod attacker-chosen files outside the project tree with Deft-managed content.

**Remediation:** apply a reusable `assertProjectionContained`-style guard to every TS init/update projection target and parent directory before read/write/mkdir/chmod operations.

---

## Acceptance

- [ ] Triage/lifecycle cache path resolution refuses when `xbrief` or `.triage-cache` is a symlink or resolves outside the project root; no out-of-tree mkdir/read/write occurs for doctor, triage:summary, or scope lifecycle writers.
- [ ] Init/update projection writers refuse when managed targets (`AGENTS.md`, `Taskfile.yml`, `.agents/`, `.githooks/`, `.github/codeql/`, `greptile.json`, `.gitattributes`, and peers) are symlinks or resolve outside the project root; no out-of-tree write/mkdir/chmod occurs.
- [ ] Shared `assertProjectionContained` (or documented twin) covers `lstat` + parent walk + project-root prefix check before every affected write path.
- [ ] Regression tests cover symlink-at-target and symlink-in-parent-path cases for both surfaces.

## Notes

Prefer one PR if the existing `#2413` containment helper can be reused on both call sites; otherwise two tightly scoped PRs in the same conflict-safe cohort are fine. This is not installer-only — the TS triage-cache and init-deposit paths are independently reachable from consumer Taskfile verbs.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
Edit these concrete paths: packages/core/src/triage/cache-path.ts, packages/core/src/init-deposit, packages/core/src/fs/projection-containment.ts, CHANGELOG.md. Verify with: pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/fs/projection-containment.test.ts packages/core/src/init-deposit. 1. Reuse assertProjectionContained on triage/lifecycle cache path resolution before mkdir/read/write.
2. Guard init/update projection writers the same way.
3. Add symlink-at-target and symlink-in-parent regression tests.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator cloning an untrusted repo, I want triage cache and init/update writers to refuse escaping symlinks, so that routine commands cannot write outside the checkout.
narratives.Traces: missing_traces_justification: bugfix / security hardening without a mapped FR id in specification.xbrief.json

narrative.Acceptance: Given a symlinked xbrief or .triage-cache escaping the project, when triage/doctor/scope cache resolution runs, then it refuses without out-of-tree writes.
Given managed projection paths that are escaping symlinks, when init/update deposit runs, then writes/mkdir/chmod are refused.
Given assertProjectionContained, when both surfaces are covered, then regression tests cover symlink-at-target and parent-path cases.
